sources.entry: Meetable - Minimal events aggregator. (Source Code) MIT PHP

summary.one_liner: Meetable is a minimal PHP/Laravel events aggregator website with tags, iCal feeds, RSVPs, and several login options.
summary.what_it_does: Meetable lists upcoming events on the home page and keeps an archive of past events. Events can carry one or more tags, and commonly used tags appear on the home page and a discover page. Every event list (home page, tag pages, etc.) has an iCal feed, and each event has an "Add to Calendar" link that exports an iCal file or links to Google Calendar. Event pages hold a cover photo, details, external and ticket links, a markdown/basic HTML description, RSVPs for logged-in users, and photos, blog posts and notes, with webmention support. An optional "Proposed Events" mode lets people vote on several candidate dates before an editor picks one.
use_cases: Run a community events calendar website
Publish a tag-organized list of meetups
Let people subscribe to event lists in their calendar app
Collect RSVPs and photos for events
Vote on possible dates for a group event
Post event reminders and listings to a Discord server
how_to_run: curl -O (download docker-compose configuration files, per README)
Set APP_KEY, APP_URL, DB_PASSWORD and DB_ROOT_PASSWORD in .env
Manual: composer install, configure .env, php artisan migrate, php artisan key:generate
Set up a queue worker (php artisan queue:listen or cron with queue:work --stop-when-empty) and the scheduler cron entry (schedule:run every minute)
notable: Multiple login methods: passkeys, GitHub OAuth, OpenID Connect, Vouch Proxy, and Heroku
Proposed Events mode where users vote on dates before one is chosen
iCal feeds for every event list and per-event add-to-calendar export
Discord bot integration for channel posts and the server event list
Webmention support so others can add photos and notes to event pages
caveats: Manual install requires PHP 8.2+, MySQL/MariaDB, and a queue worker plus scheduler cron job
Docker setup binds the port only to localhost, so a TLS reverse proxy is needed for public access
Heroku login is described as meant for a single user and hard to configure later
